purpose: Define the scope of the completed eight-case factorial audit and its relationship to the original six-deletion correlation. Read-only comparison; no fixtures, model weights or generations changed.

observations.original_training_prompts: Exactly six pure-deletion concern rows win66582; the other14 concern rows and all20 clean rows win788 at selected update100.
observations.original_replay: All40 shared continuations repeat the archive byte-for-byte and all40 actual first sampled IDs equal teacher argmax.
observations.new_factorial: All8 shared continuations begin788 and copy changed-line text. Retaining an effective guard and changing deletion to no-op replacement do not separate that first ID. No response explains the harm mechanism.

serialization_result: The original and new prompts share byte-identical system messages, ChatML role framing, repository/rule/changed-line headings and final output instruction. The audit uses the host constructor, while training uses stored messages, but these two routes produce the same prompt format. The substantive transfer changes are user-content expansion and wording, rather than a different chat template.
what_current_factorial_holds_fixed: Within each four-case context block: model, shared prefix and its three IDs, system text, ChatML framing, repository/path/title, description, rule and final output instruction.
Shape comparison at a fixed harm label: the deleted candidate guard is replaced by (void)0, leaving behavior unchanged.
Harm comparison at a fixed shape: the clean example retains another effective identical guard; the harmful example has only the changed guard.
Decoding within the audit: greedy temperature0, continuation limit192, two threads and floating activations.
what_current_factorial_changes: Across original versus expanded audit: descriptions explicitly name the consequence and state that checks are fully shown.
Across original versus expanded audit: partial hunks become full functions with declarations/includes and enclosing braces; prompt length and attention positions change.
Across original versus expanded audit: hunk starts and physical cited line numbers change to the new function coordinates.
Within the present audit clean/harm contrast: inserting an earlier guard also shifts the changed guard from physical line5 to6. These metadata changes accompany the intended semantic contrast.

context_argument_source_audit.effect: The argument controls token-ID allocation capacity and input/output budget validation. Both prompts fit within2048. It is not passed as an inference position, RoPE scale, or architecture parameter.

evidence.detail: Checks model maximum context; allocates context+1 IDs and rejects prompt/output overflow.
KV cache length is n+max_tokens, independent of the configured context argument for identical token input.
Forward positions derive from token count and loop position.
RoPE base comes from GGUF metadata; rotation uses each actual token position.

context_argument_source_audit.conclusion: The2048-to8192 bookkeeping difference supplies no mechanism for a different first-token decision on these bounded prompts.

scope_of_conclusion: The original six-for-six association remains an exact observation on the original training prompts. The expanded factorial shows that its token preference does not transfer unchanged to these two richer contexts, and that these contexts produce changed-line copying across both harm labels and shapes. Because original-to-audit content changes occur together, this comparison does not attribute the shift from66582 to788 to deletion shape alone.

smallest_next_control.status: Proposed only; no implementation or generation.
